verdict.rationale: mise's first-party docs cover the whole story. Developers declare per-project tool versions in a checked-in mise.toml, which also accepts .tool-versions and idiomatic version files. `mise use` and `mise install` install the tools, and mise switches versions automatically as you change directories, with lockfiles available for reproducibility. Multiple independent community users corroborate replacing nvm, rvm and pyenv with mise for per-project, team-wide toolchains.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install and switch language runtimes or tool versions per project from a checked-in config file

citations.quote: Keep multiple versions of Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, and other tools on the same machine, then declare which ones a project uses in `mise.toml`.
`mise use` installs Node.js 24 if needed and records the request in a new `mise.toml`
mise automatically switches between them as you move between the two projects
mise replaces them with one file that's checked in, so a fresh laptop is `git clone` and `mise bootstrap`.
mise is also compatible with asdf `.tool-versions` files and with idiomatic version files like `.node-version` and `.ruby-version`.
Being able to have one config file to manage tools (node, python, rust, go, etc) as well as a simple makefile replacement makes it incredibly convenient.
